- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral; model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.3), model often overreacts; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < -0.15), model fails to adjust downward; apply mean reversion correction to last 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; delay correction by 1–2 days if sentiment changes direction.
- Forecast mean tends to be 2–3% higher than true outcome; apply 2–3% downward adjustment for 30-day horizon.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope for next 5 days.
